newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea warns against more N.Korean provocations.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea warns against more N.Korean provocations.

text.p: South Korea, saying North Korea has massed long-range artillery and fighters near their border in recent years, warned on Thursday against more military provocations by the communist country.

President Kim Young-sam told a meeting of military leaders that a September intrusion by a North Korean submarine into South Korean waters illustrated Pyongyang's intention of trying to take the South by force.
"The people, government and military must be united in one and be fully prepared to instantly counter any North Korean provocation," Kim's spokesman quoted the president as saying.
"Without security -- politics, economy and democratic welfare are all like castles built on sand," he was quoted as saying.

Kim was speaking after military leaders said North Korea had massed weapons and troops near the Demilitarized Zone since its "Great Leader" Kim Il-sung died in 1994. The zone separates the Korean peninsula.
The two Koreas have been technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce, rather than a peace treaty.

A military spokesman said that military leaders told the meeting that the impoverished North Korea focused its resources on building up its war machines despite an acute food shortage and economic difficulties.

North Korea has built about 500 underground tunnels near the border since last year to store military equipment, while increasing navy and air force exercises by 30 percent and 34 percent respectively since Kim Il-sung's death.
Kim Jong-il, Kim Il-sung's son, has taken control of the Stalinist state since his father's death but has yet to be confirmed as the state's president and head of the ruling Workers Party.
The North Korean military doubled the number of 240mm multiple rocket launchers to 280 from 140 and that of 170mm self-propelled guns to 500 from 300 since 1994, the military spokesman said.

The North also increased the size of the special forces to 110,000 from 100,000 during the period. About 40,000 of them could be infiltrated to the South by submarines, helicopters and hydrofoils at the same time now, instead of 20,000 previously, he added.

The South Korean president on Thursday again renewed demands for an apology from North Korea for the submarine incursion and said Seoul would not resume any economic assistance to the North unless it agreed to direct dialogue.
Tensions on the Korean peninsula have worsened since the submarine landed 26 agents on a South Korean beach in September. Pyongyang says the incident was an accident.
All but two of the 26 were shot dead. One was captured alive and another is still missing.
